summary: Descendants and the spouse are guaranteed half of their intestate share, with a smaller share for parents and other close relatives. Serbia has no trust law and is outside the Hague Trusts Convention. Foundations serve public benefit.
reserved_share: Descendants, adoptees and spouse: 1/2 of the intestate share; parents and other heirs 1/3 (1/2 if permanently unable to work); Law on Succession (OG 46/1995, 101/2003, 6/2015). Article numbers not confirmed.
foreign_law_note: The 1982 Law on Conflict of Laws applied the deceased's national law to succession, with Serbian law for Serbian immovables. There was no free choice. Whether a newer private international law act changed this was not checked.
trust_note: No trust law. Law on Endowments and Foundations (2010) allows foundations for public-benefit goals.
open_questions: Statute article numbers and exact fractions for forced heirs outside descendants and spouse were not read in the primary text; confirm in the official gazette.
Whether a foreign national resident may choose a law for their estate under the current private international law act was not confirmed.
A draft civil code is under preparation.
